title: High Pressing System
content: High pressing is a defensive tactic where a team maintains a very high defensive line, positioning defenders close to the opponent's penalty area to apply immediate pressure on the ball carrier. This approach aims to win the ball back in advanced positions, limiting the opponent's time and space to organize their attack. It can be executed using man-to-man marking, zonal defense, or a hybrid model, requiring high fitness levels and coordinated team movement to maintain compactness. The primary objective is to force turnovers in dangerous areas, creating immediate scoring opportunities or preventing the opponent from building structured play. This system is most effective when the team has the physical capacity to sustain intense pressure and when the opponent is vulnerable to high-intensity defensive actions. Coaches must ensure that the defensive line remains coordinated to avoid being exposed to counter-attacks if the press is bypassed.
